description:
Compare U.S. airline pet policies side by side: one-way in-cabin fee, carrier dimensions, weight limit, cargo availability and large-dog cabin options.
Answers comparison questions such as "Which airlines charge under $100 for a dog?", "Which U.S. airlines allow pets in cargo?" or "Compare Delta, Alaska and Southwest pet policies"; it does not check ticket prices, flight schedules or availability.
All filters are optional; calling with no filters returns all covered U.S. airlines sorted by lowest in-cabin fee. Each row carries its official source URLs and verified date.

airlines.description: Specific airlines to compare by id, name or IATA code, e.g. ["Delta", "Alaska", "Southwest"]

cargo_only.description: Only airlines that accept general public pets in checked baggage or cargo

dog_weight_lb.description: Filter out airlines whose stated in-cabin weight cap is below this dog weight in pounds

large_dog_cabin.description: Only airlines with a stated in-cabin option for large dogs without an under-seat carrier

max_fee_usd.description: Maximum one-way in-cabin pet fee in US dollars

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

name: dogpolicies_compare_airlines

accepted.description: With bad_input: each argument that could not be read, with the values it accepts

code.description: With an outcome other than ok: not_found, invalid, unavailable

did_you_mean.description: Close matches to what was asked for: towns, places, slugs or brands, best first

nearest.description: When nothing is inside the radius: the nearest places in the data, with distance_miles

next.description: Calls that would answer the question, in words

outcome.description: Absent or ok: a normal answer. no_match: nothing in the data matches, see did_you_mean, nearest and next. bad_input: the arguments cannot be used as given, see next. partial: some of the ids were found, see missing. unavailable: a live source could not be read. None of these is an error.

resolved_from.description: Set when a word was read as the value the tool uses: hotel as lodging, NB as north. Each key is the argument; asked is what was sent, used what it was read as

title: Compare U.S. airline pet policies
